Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Per our call, I put together a short recap and the immediate technical questions your security team flagged so we can move to a technical deep dive next week. Attaching our high-level security controls and a data retention matrix for reference.

Recap (high level):
- Use case: FintechCo will send production request/response payloads to Redwood for model inference in a mix of hosted + dedicated environments.
- Key concerns: PII in logs (cardholder data, SSNs, email/mobile), request/response logging, header metadata (trace IDs, customer identifiers), retention windows, and data residency for logs.
- Ask from FintechCo: examples of redaction/masking capabilities, whether we log request/response bodies or headers by default, where logs are stored, and configuration for retention and deletion.

Security team questions (please see bolded items we discussed):
1) Do you persist raw request/response bodies by default? If so, for how long and where?
2) Can we disable request/response logging entirely for specific routes or customers?
3) What redaction options exist for headers (trace IDs, x-correlation-id) and for free-text PII detection?
4) Can we provide an audit log showing redaction events and who accessed logs?
5) Data residency: can logs be kept in a US-only region (us-east-1) for this workload?
6) KMS/HSM and key separation for any stored logs.

Attachments: redwood_security_controls.pdf, data_retention_matrix.xlsx, example-logging-config.txt

Next steps I propose:
- Technical deep dive with Dev Patel + David Kim (30-45m) to walk through config options and a sample config for your routes.
- Provide a short config sample that demonstrates disabling request/response logging and header scrubbing.
- Share SOC 2 snapshot and confirmation on KMS options (if needed).

Are you available for a 30-45m technical call next week (Tue/Wed preferred PDT)?

Hi Alice / team —

Wanted to answer the specific technical items before the call so you have context. Short answers up front:
- Default logging: In Redwood's hosted API we capture request/response metadata for observability by default (latency, token usage, status codes). We do NOT persist raw request/response bodies unless a customer enables request/response logging or uses a Dedicated/Private setup with logging enabled.
- Encryption & residency: Any persisted logs are encrypted at rest with AES-256. For hosted customers that opt into persisted logs we can restrict storage to a single region (us-east-1) for enterprise agreements or handle via Dedicated/Private deployment to guarantee residency.
- Per-customer overrides: Yes. We expose per-route/per-customer logging policies. You can set logging_level: none | metadata | full. Setting logging_level: none prevents request/response bodies from being written to disk while still emitting metrics.
- Header & trace ID handling: We support header scrubbing rules (regex-based) and inline redaction hooks. For trace IDs we recommend hashing (SHA-256 trunc) at ingest so you preserve a correlation key without storing the raw value.
- PII detection & redaction: We provide configurable detectors (PII patterns + ML-based entity detection) and policy-driven redaction prior to any storage. Redaction events are recorded in an audit log (metadata only) showing field patterns matched + timestamp + redaction_type. The audit log itself is append-only and access-controlled.
- Audit trail: Access to logs and redaction records is tracked via our access logs and can be exported to your SIEM. For high-security customers we support pushing audit events to your Kinesis/Splunk endpoint.
- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS for hosted logs and HSM-backed keys for Private deployments.

Example config snippet (example-logging-config.txt attached):

# per-route policy example
route: /v1/fintechco/*
logging_level: none # disables request/response persistence
header_scrub: ["x-correlation-id", "authorization"]
trace_id_strategy: hash_truncate
pii_redaction: ["email", "ssn", "credit_card"]
retention_days: 30

If you'd like, on the call we can walk through the attached example and show a demo of turning logging_level between metadata/full/none for a sandbox route.
